seo.title: Redact PDF — Permanently Remove Sensitive Content | JPdf
seo.description: Black out sensitive text or images in a PDF for real — the covered content is permanently removed, not just hidden underneath a box. Free, fast, and private.

subtitle: Permanently remove sensitive content from a PDF — not just cover it up.

howItWorks.title: How to redact a PDF
steps: Upload the PDF containing sensitive content.
Draw a black box over each area you want removed.
Click Export to download a PDF where that content is genuinely gone.

editor.overlayNote: Redaction boxes are shown in black while you work — nothing is actually removed until you export.
editor.destructiveNote: Any page with a redaction box is converted to a flattened image so the covered content can't be recovered — that page's text will no longer be selectable or searchable in the exported PDF.

items.q: Does this actually remove the content, or just draw over it?
items.a: It actually removes it. Any page you redact is converted into a flattened image with the black boxes burned directly into the pixels — there's no hidden text or image left underneath to recover by deleting a shape or copying text, the way there would be with a simple drawn rectangle.

A redacted page becomes a static image, so its text is no longer selectable, searchable, or copyable in the exported file — a necessary trade-off for a genuine guarantee that the covered content is gone. Pages without any redaction keep their original text and quality.

items.q: Can I undo a redaction before exporting?
items.a: Yes — nothing is permanent until you export. Use undo/redo or delete a box like any other element while you're working.

items.q: Will my file be kept private?
items.a: Yes. Your file is marked up in your browser and only uploaded when you click Export; results are processed securely and automatically deleted after a short retention period.
